primary_full_report.rationale: This is a 14-page primary research article formulating RUVA as a Dec-POMDP with MARL centralized policy gradients and evaluating it empirically.
primary_full_report.quote: In this paper, we propose a novel reliability-aware video analytics scheme for multi-UAV-assisted systems (RUVA).

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section VI-A deploys the system on three DJI drones with Manifold onboard computers plus an edge-cloud server for profiling and multi-UAV MARL evaluation.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: We deployed our proposed solution in a UAV-assisted video analytics system. There were three Da-Jiang Innovations drones equipped with the Manifold platform, which is a UAV-onboard edge computing device.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Multi-agent UAVs jointly coordinate task offloading decisions, frame resolution adaptation, and DNN object-detection model selection with a shared edge server.
collaborative_inference.quote: We adopt a reliability formulation based on the Poisson failure assumption, and formulate the video analytics services as an optimization problem which jointly optimizes offloading decision, frame resolution and deep neural network model selection

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section VI evaluates four object-detection DNNs profiled on physical drone/edge hardware across five video resolutions and compares against six baselines over 20,000 MARL episodes.
evaluative_evidence.quote: In our simulation, the computation capacity, computation delay, accuracy rate, etc. were all directly profiled and measured from the physical hardware. Tables II-IV represent actual measurements.

primary_full_report.quote: Therefore, in this paper, we design a joint optimization framework based on Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C) and proximal policy optimization (PPO).

collaborative_inference.quote: The DNN model is partitioned into two parts: the front part is executed locally on the intelligent terminal, and the intermediate feature results are transmitted to the UAV, where the remaining part is executed by the UAV of edge server.

evaluative_evidence.quote: The effectiveness of the proposed A3C-PPO hybrid architecture is verified through comparative experiments. Two baseline strategies are constructed for evaluation. The bandwidth allocation strategy based on A3C is denoted as Only-A3C.

primary_full_report.quote: In this paper, we propose A3D, an edge server assisted drone navigation framework that can dynamically adjust task execution location, input resolution, and image compression ratio

evaluative_evidence.quote: To further investigate the performance of A3D’s resource allocation with more drones, we carry out numerical simulations using the data traces collected from real drones.

primary_full_report.quote: We propose a deadline-driven heuristic, DEMS-A, to schedule diverse DNN tasks generated continuously to perform inferencing over video segments generated by multiple drones linked to an edge, with the option to execute on the cloud.

records.title: NetMoE: Joint Trajectory Planning and Distributed Mixture-of-Experts Inference for UAV Swarms

identity_evidence.quote: This article has been accepted for publication in IEEE Internet of Things Journal. This is the author's version which has not been fully edited and content may change prior to final publication. Citation information: DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2026.3755315

primary_full_report.rationale: This is an 18-page primary research article presenting NetMoE with mathematical system formulation, router/planner design, and simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: We propose the NetMoE, an abstract expert-assignment framework which couples a connectivity-aware centralized online trajectory planner with a learnable topology-aware router inspired by the need for accurate expert assignment in target search tasks on UAV swarms.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluated in a 10-UAV FANET swarm simulation (Table III, Sec. VI) and swarm-size sweeps from 6 to 50 UAVs.

collaborative_inference.quote: Each UAV hosts a single dedicated DNN expert model of type ei. Since the onboard memory and compute of an individual UAV cannot accommodate all M experts, the experts are distributed across the swarm rather than co-located on one node.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluated over 300 test episodes across 3 seeds against layer-wise partitioning, heuristic/accuracy-only routers, and MARL/sweep planners, plus CIFAR-100 complexity/accuracy measurements.
evaluative_evidence.quote: Table VI supplements the per-inference comparison with modeled inference workload, payload volume, movement-command traffic, and resource utilization over 3 seeds × 100 episodes.

records.title: A DRL-Assisted Decentralized Framework for UAV Swarm Collaborative Inference

identity_evidence.quote: This article has been accepted for publication in IEEE Internet of Things Journal. This is the author's version which has not been fully edited and content may change prior to final publication. Citation information: DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2026.3740035

primary_full_report.rationale: This is a 16-page primary research article presenting DDCI with POMDP/DRL design, analytical pipeline model, and multi-architecture simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: To address this, we propose DDCI, a decentralized collaborative inference framework in which each UAV autonomously selects a collaboration partner and a DNN partition point through a locally executed deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policy.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluated in a custom Gymnasium simulation of N=10 heterogeneous UAVs communicating over 802.11ac (Sec. V-A) plus sensitivity sweeps over swarm size.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The swarm comprises N= 10 UAVs with heterogeneous compute capacities Ci ∈ {160,320,400,600,800} GFLOPS, corresponding to embedded UAV processors ranging from low-power modules to high-end accelerators (Section V-A), communicating over Wi-Fi 802.11ac within radius R comm = 200m.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Each UAV performs layer-wise partitioning across four DNN models (Part A locally, intermediate features over air-to-air links to Pareto-selected neighbor UAVs for Part B) with MiniBatch pipelining and link-interruption recovery.
collaborative_inference.quote: A swarm of UAVs performs real-time DNN inference over a disaster area without ground infrastructure. Each UAV partitions the DNN model and collaborates with a selected neighbor through air-to-air communication to accelerate inference.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section V evaluates DDCI across YOLOv5m, VGG-16, VGG-19, and GoogLeNet-22 over 30 episodes against six baselines, with sensitivity sweeps and frozen-policy ablations.
evaluative_evidence.quote: To isolate the contribution of each design component, we conduct an ablation on VGG-16 with N=10, R comm=200m over 30 episodes (Table VII).
